## 29.9.3

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.9.3 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.9.3)
- [moby/moby, 29.9.3 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.9.3)

### Security

This release includes fixes for multiple security vulnerabilities affecting Docker Engine and related components.

- **CVE-2026-116587** Fix possible excessive CPU usage when parsing crafted RSA keys  
  [GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q)
- **CVE-2026-116591** Fix a possible panic when decompressing zstd data  
  [GHSA-fpmh-frq8-7rj8](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fpmh-frq8-7rj8)
- **CVE-2026-115538** Fix missing encryption and spoofing protections for Swarm overlay networks after firewalld flushes Docker's iptables rules  
  [GHSA-6jhp-7446-hf7f](https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-6jhp-7446-hf7f)

The SwarmKit update fixes the following security vulnerability:

- **CVE-2026-115539** Fix a vulnerability where an attacker with a valid worker-node TLS certificate and private key could obtain a manager-node certificate shortly after a Swarm leader change  
  [GHSA-628g-hv7f-pgjc](https://github.com/moby/swarmkit/security/advisories/GHSA-628g-hv7f-pgjc)

The [BuildKit v0.34.2 update](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/tag/v0.34.2) fixes the following security vulnerabilities:

- [GHSA-2fqp-xg6f-v7gj](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-2fqp-xg6f-v7gj): A build that resolved metadata for the same Git source reference twice could crash the daemon through resolver cache poisoning.  
- [GHSA-w26x-xg27-7qjc](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-w26x-xg27-7qjc): A malicious client with access to the BuildKit control APIs could set extended attributes on files outside the BuildKit state directory, potentially granting elevated privileges to programs on the host.  

### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Fix literal `<<` keys in YAML files being emitted without quotes. [docker/cli#7461](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7461)
- Fix the daemon hanging on container, image, and system API requests under load. [moby/moby#54041](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54041)
- Update BuildKit to [v0.34.2](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/tag/v0.34.2). [moby/moby#54107](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54107)

## Highlights - **OIDC step-up authentication**: Apps can request `acr_values` and `max_age` and read `acr`, `amr`, and `auth_time` from tokens. Account Center uses it to require a recent sign-in before sensitive changes. - **Sign-In with Ethereum**: A new Ethereum Wallet social connector lets users sign in with an EVM wallet. - **Keep the iOS "Save Password" prompt**: The `confirm_redirect_policy` sign-in parameter shows a "Continue" page before returning to the app after the user enters a password. - **Personal access tokens in Account Center**: Users can create, rename, and revoke their own personal access tokens. - **GeeTest CAPTCHA**: Use GeeTest CAPTCHA v4 for bot protection, which suits sign-in experiences targeting mainland China. - **Static attributes for SAML applications**: Send fixed attribute values in every SAML assertion. - **Security fixes, one needing admin action**: This release includes security fixes for MFA, social and enterprise sign-in, the Account API, and Logto Tunnel. Standard OAuth 2.0 and Microsoft Azure AD social connectors need a settings review after upgrading. See **Security hardening** below. ## New features & enhancements ### OIDC step-up authentication OIDC clients can now ask for a recent or stronger sign-in: - **Request**: Pass `acr_values` and `max_age` in the authorization request. Logto advertises the supported ACR values in the discovery document. - **Result**: `acr`, `amr`, and `auth_time` are returned in ID tokens, access tokens, and introspection responses. - **Account Center**: The built-in Account Center now authorizes sensitive Account API operations with a fresh first-party `urn:logto:acr:1fa` access token instead of a separate verification record. When the sign-in is not recent enough, the Account API answers with an RFC 9470 step-up challenge. - **Recent authentication window**: Set how recent the sign-in must be in **Console > Sign-in experience > Account center > Recent authentication** (10 minutes by default). A client can still request a shorter window with `max_age`. - **Compatibility**: Apps that call the Account API directly can still use a verification record ID for sensitive operations. See [Step-up authentication](https://docs.logto.io/end-user-flows/step-up-authentication). ### Sign-In with Ethereum Admins can enable the new Ethereum Wallet social connector (`@logto/connector-siwe`). Users with an injected EIP-1193 wallet sign a one-time SIWE (EIP-4361) message without leaving the sign-in page. A single address works across supported EVM chains, and admins can restrict the allowed chain IDs. ### Keep the iOS "Save Password" prompt On iOS, `ASWebAuthenticationSession` closes as soon as it sees the app's callback URL, which dismisses the system "Save Password" prompt right after the user signs in with a password. Pass `confirm_redirect_policy=password` in the authorization request to show a page that returns to the app only when the user selects "Continue". The page appears after the user enters a password in the sign-in experience: password sign-in, password registration, setting a password, or a step-up password verification. Without the parameter, Logto redirects back to the app right away. Third-party applications ignore it. The Swift integration guide in Console shows how to use it. See [Keep the iOS Save Password prompt](https://docs.logto.io/end-user-flows/authentication-parameters#keep-the-ios-save-password-prompt). ### Personal access tokens in Account Center When the tenant enables the personal access token field in Account Center, users can create, rename, and revoke personal access tokens on the Account Center **Security** page. Each token is shown only once at creation and expires within 365 days. The same operations are available through the Account API under `/api/my-account/personal-access-tokens`, with the new `urn:logto:scope:personal_access_tokens` scope (`UserScope.PersonalAccessTokens` in `@logto/core-kit`). ### GeeTest CAPTCHA [GeeTest](https://www.geetest.com) CAPTCHA v4 is now available as a CAPTCHA provider. Its adaptive challenges are localized, which suits sign-in experiences targeting mainland China, where Google reCAPTCHA is often unreachable. 1. Create a CAPTCHA v4 event in the GeeTest dashboard. 2. Go to **Console > Security > CAPTCHA** and add GeeTest with its CAPTCHA ID and CAPTCHA key. The same configuration is available through `PUT /api/captcha-provider` with `type: "Geetest"`. While GeeTest is the CAPTCHA provider, the sign-in page's Content Security Policy allows GeeTest's SDK, API, and static hosts. ### `access_denied` when sign-in is cancelled - **Consent page**: Cancelling the built-in consent page now ends the interaction with `access_denied` and returns the user to the client application with the original `state` and `iss`. - **Direct sign-in**: A failed direct sign-in returns to the client the same way, instead of falling back to the hosted sign-in page. - **Custom sign-in experiences**: End the current interaction with the same error through `POST /api/experience/abort`, with an optional `reason` that becomes `error_description`. `GET /api/experience/interaction/direct-sign-in` returns the `direct_sign_in` value of the current authorization request, so a custom experience can tell a direct sign-in from a hosted one before the interaction is initialized. ### User management - **Require MFA setup for a user**: Turn on **Require MFA setup** on the user details page in Console, or set `mfa.required` to `true` through the Management API. ### Security fixes

- win32: restrict loading plugin dependencies (DLLs) to plugin, app
  and system directories.

- win32: run openvpn.exe from the interactive service at "high integrity
  level", that is, process memory of openvpn.exe and all its threads are
  protected from tampering.  Signals/Events are still permitted.

- win32: openvpnserv: strictly filter user-defined environment variables
  before passing to openvpn.exe ([CVE-2026-121720](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-121720))

  (Issue found by @refiaa, tracked in
   Github: OpenVPN/openvpn-private-issues#186)

- win32: openvpnserv: make validation of openvpn command line more robust
  to invalid-quoting attacks ([CVE-2026-115342](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-115342))

- win32: openvpn.exe: change parsing of commandline to use the same
  function that the interactive service uses (`CommandLineToArgvW()`)
  ([CVE-2026-115342](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-115342))

  (Issues found by Heiko Hund, tracked in
   Github: OpenVPN/openvpn-private-issues#184)

### Bug fixes

- Username/Password parsing from `--auth-user-pass` file (or inline)
  left parts of overlong usernames in the password field.  Fix.
  (GH [OpenVPN/openvpn#1140](https://github.com/OpenVPN/openvpn/issues/1140))

- win32: openvpnserv: fix memory leak for security descriptors

- win32: repair logging of errors in Windows `tun_read_queue()`

- win32: avoid accessing uninitialized structure data if `GetInterfaceInfo()`
  or `GetPerAdapterInfo()` fail

- win32: openvpnserv: avoid double `free()` if `GetTokenInformation()` fails

- win32: openvpnserv: avoid potential format-string issue on registry defaults

- win32: openvpnserv: repair error reporting on `RegGetValueA()` failures
  inside `GetItfDnsServersV4()`

- win32: openvpnserv: fix `inet_ntop()` return code check in
  `GetItfDnsServersV6()`, making it ignore DHCP-provided DNS servers.

- route: repair printing of ROUTE_GATEWAY/ROUTE6_GATEWAY info - the actual gateway handling was correct, just not
  printing anything anymore.

- config: check_file_access: fix `--extra-certs` access check

- win32: tun: free gc arena in `windows_set_mtu()` (mem leak in error path)

- route: close socket in Haiku `get_default_gateway()` (FD leak)

- win32: openvpnserv: skip conversion of empty domain names

- win32: cmake+mingw: don't prefix the event message DLL with lib
  (it was building 'libopenvpnservmsg.dll' instead of 'openvpnservmsg.dll')

- win32: pass the buffer size in bytes to `get_openvpn_reg_value()`

- PUSH_UPDATE server: free temporary options after sending message (memleak)


### User-visible Changes

- Linux: set `IFF_BACKPRESSURE` on Linux (if available)

  This helps the kernel tun/tap to apply proper prioritization (qdisc etc)
  to incoming packets if userspace is slow to process them.  Without the
  flag, the kernel would just drop everything.

- Management/GUI: Optionally indicate username in `>PASSWORD '<UP_TYPE>'` prompts

  If an openvpn config has a username set but no password, and OpenVPN
  wants to prompt for the password, the GUI could not see the username
  today and prompted for both.  With this change, OpenVPN sends a hint to
  the management interface, so a GUI can pre-fill the username field, or
  only prompt for the password.

  This is only done if the management interface client announces
  support for it (compatibility level >= 6).

### Code improvements/general hardening

- crypto_epoch: wipe key material with `secure_memzero()`

- do not look up "none" cipher in OpenSSL - this avoids leaving an "error"
  on the OpenSSL error stack, which can then later lead to spurious
  SSL error prints on CRL loading.

- Make CRL reload EOF detection independent of stale error queue entries
  (GH: [OpenVPN/openvpn#1104](https://github.com/OpenVPN/openvpn/issues/1104))

- tls_crypt: fix handling of "cipher final output" (which is always empty
  on today's SSL libraries, so no impact today, but might not be in future)

- crypto: `ASSERT()` opt before first use in `openvpn_decrypt_aead()`

- auth_token: wipe the server secret key after loading it

- port-share: do not write journal file through symlinks or hardlinks
  (and also document how port-share directory should be set up)
  (GH [OpenVPN/openvpn#1124](https://github.com/OpenVPN/openvpn/issues/1124))

- dns-updown: close first pipe if creating the second one fails
  (avoid leaking file descriptors on error)

- init: check parameters for NULL before strlen() in send_cc_message
  (not triggerable today)

- crypto_openssl: Clear PEM decoded key data before freeing it

- Increase the buffer size for alert-message in management user-pass query
  (so long usernames can be hinted towards the GUI)

- win32: openvpnserv: validate message size for dns/nrpt/wins handlers
  (GH: [OpenVPN/openvpn#1129](https://github.com/OpenVPN/openvpn/issues/1129))

- win32: plugin: detect too long plugin paths on Windows

- win32: openvpnserv: null-terminate iface.name in address and route handlers
  (GH: [OpenVPN/openvpn#1130](https://github.com/OpenVPN/openvpn/issues/1130))


### Documentation improvements

- Fix numbering of examples in management-notes.txt

- Document "notify" as auth pending method

- Convert Changes.rst to Markdown (2.7)


### Long-term code maintenance

- OpenSSL 4.1 compatibility: use `ASN1_STRING_get_length()` now, providing
  a fallback to `ASN1_STRING_length()` for older SSL libraries.

- Linux: sitnl: use `RTM_SETLINK` for updating existing interfaces
  (instead of `RTM_NEWLINK`)

- gen-sample-keys.sh: Don't apply server extensions to CSRs

- review all usages of `strncpy()`
  (change to `strncpynt()`, `memcpy()`, etc. where appropriate)

This is a quick follow-up on top of 2.11.8, to fix a regression it introduced and a few more security issues, mostly in FastCGI. It contains only fixes backported from master, plus a couple of small additions. **If you're on 2.11.8 and serve PHP, we recommend upgrading.**

**Huge thank you to our sponsors for keeping the project alive with resources, and for our maintainers who triage and assist tirelessly in this relentless new age of AI.**

## Highlights

- **Fixed: PHP directory indexes (regression in 2.11.8).** A request for a directory with a trailing slash, like `/wp-admin/`, was matched by the directory itself instead of its `index.php`, so it never reached PHP and usually got a 404. This broke WordPress admin pages and other apps that serve an index through a trailing-slash URL. A `try_files` pattern now only matches a directory when it ends in `/`. Thanks @dunglas! (#8352)
- **Path matchers with placeholders** now work as expected: placeholders like `{env.FOO}` are no longer lower-cased into `{env.foo}` before they're looked up, and their values are compared case-insensitively against the request path, like static patterns. Thanks @BenMacha! (#8343)
- **New `plain_time_format` option for [`file_server browse`](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/file_server):** sets the time layout of plain-text directory listings (`Accept: text/plain`). Thanks @steffenbusch! (#8084)
- **Fewer allocations** in path cleaning, header rewriting and `weighted_round_robin` selection. Thanks @jvoisin! (#7842)
- **For plugin authors:** new `httpcaddyfile.Helper.IsNamedRoute()` tells a directive whether it's being parsed inside a [named route](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/concepts#named-routes). (#8354)

## :warning: Breaking changes

- **Conflicting `client_auth` is now a Caddyfile error.** When two site blocks share TLS connection policies for the same hostname but set different `client_auth`, the adapter used to keep the first one and silently drop the other, which could quietly remove a stricter mTLS requirement. (#8306)
- **FastCGI requests that are ambiguous about which script they run get `400`:**
  - when the escaped path (which `%`-containing path matchers see) and the decoded path would select different scripts, e.g. `/public/tool.php%2f..%2f..%2fadmin%2ftool.php` (#8357)
  - on Windows, script paths with an 8.3 short name component (like `ADMINI~1`) or a `:` (NTFS alternate data streams) (#8356)
- **FastCGI `env` values now take precedence over request headers**, so a client can no longer override `HTTP_*` variables you set with `env` (see below). (#8358)

## Security fixes

Thank you to everyone who reported responsibly and helped with patches:

- fastcgi: A client could override any `HTTP_*` variable set with the FastCGI transport's (or `php_fastcgi`'s) `env` subdirective by sending a matching request header, for example choosing the user an application sees in `HTTP_X_AUTH_USER`. Configured values now win. Reported by @JebeenLee and @Camel4, fixed by @dunglas. (GHSA-q34h-28rj-5hjm, #8358)
- fastcgi: On Windows, NTFS 8.3 short names and alternate data streams could run a script that a path rule was meant to deny, completing the FastCGI fix from 2.11.8. Thanks @dunglas. (GHSA-9cr8-wmhh-39pm, #8356)
- fastcgi: Encoded slashes and dot segments could make a `%`-containing path matcher approve one script while another one runs. Thanks @dunglas. (#8357)
- fastcgi: Over HTTP/2, a `host` field sent next to `:authority` could make the application see a different host (`HTTP_HOST`) than the one Caddy routed the request to. Thanks @dunglas. (#8355)
- httpcaddyfile: A stricter `client_auth` could be silently dropped when merging TLS connection policies (see above). Thanks @sam-kota. (#8306)
- Updated `go-jose` to v4.1.6 for GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q. (#8299)

:warning: These security patches may be breaking if your application relies on the buggy behaviors.

# ProxySQL 3.0.12 Release Notes

Release date: 2026-11-05

ProxySQL 3.0.12 improves the reliability of applications that use ProxySQL to route database traffic. It fixes cases where a connection failure could cause earlier statements in a batch to run twice, where transaction state could be lost during error recovery, and where malformed client packets could compromise the proxy. The release addresses eight published security advisories.

It also extends causal-read routing to MariaDB, allowing applications to select a replica that has caught up with a required transaction, and adds subnet matching to query rules so operators can apply routing policies to groups of client addresses.

## Highlights

- **Safer query retries:** a batch is not replayed on another backend after an earlier result has already reached the application, preventing duplicate execution of those statements.
- **MariaDB support for causal reads:** routing now understands MariaDB transaction identifiers as well as MySQL GTIDs, helping applications avoid reading a replica before a required write has arrived.
- **Eight security advisories fixed:** bounds checks and protocol validation address four high-severity and four medium-severity issues shared by all three release tiers.
- **More reliable PostgreSQL sessions:** authentication, transaction recovery, prepared statements, and connection cleanup receive correctness fixes.
- **Subnet-based query rules:** client and proxy address conditions can match IPv4 and IPv6 network prefixes rather than requiring a rule for each address.
- **Updated platform support:** Ubuntu 26.04 packages are available for both architectures, and the release embeds OpenSSL 3.5.7.

## New Features

### MariaDB transaction identifiers for causal reads

Applications often write to a primary server and send subsequent reads to replicas. Replication takes time: choosing a replica without checking its progress can return data that predates the application's write. Causal-read routing uses a transaction identifier to select a replica that has reached the required position.

ProxySQL now understands MariaDB's `domain-server-sequence` identifiers alongside MySQL's `UUID:sequence` identifiers. For MariaDB, it compares the sequence watermark within the relevant domain. Transaction positions retain their database-specific format in reader updates and statistics. (#6222.)

MariaDB positions can be learned from successful server responses that contain transaction tracking information. When tracking is requested through `mysql-default_session_track_gtids=OWN_GTID` or by the client, ProxySQL adds MariaDB's `last_gtid` tracking while preserving other tracked variables. It does not send an extra blocking query to discover the write position. The integration uses binlog reader 2.5.0. (#6275, #6228.)

This routing still depends on correctly configured tracking and replica-progress information. MySQL routing for a tracked single-UUID set uses its highest transaction ID and assumes transactions are applied in commit order; it does not establish complete set containment for out-of-order or multi-UUID replication. (#6461.)

Keep freshness-sensitive queries out of the text-query cache: a cache hit can return an existing TTL-cached result without waiting for the required transaction or replication-lag condition.

### Subnet matching in query rules

Routing policies frequently apply to a service network or a group of clients rather than to one IP address. Query rules can now use CIDR network prefixes in `client_addr` and `proxy_addr`, avoiding a separate rule for every address in the subnet.

The implementation supports IPv4, IPv6, and normalized IPv4-mapped addresses. Existing literal-address matching continues to work. (#6223, #6259.)

### Queued MySQL commands

Some clients send the next command before reading the preceding response. ProxySQL now queues complete commands and executes them in order, including prepared execution and `COM_PING`. It pauses further input when queued commands or pending output need to be drained. Applications receive responses in the same order as their requests. (#6470, #6511.)

Entering permanent replication forwarding while commands remain queued is rejected by closing that client connection. This prevents already-received commands from being stranded during the transition. (#6579.)

### PostgreSQL authentication with stored credentials

Deployments that manage PostgreSQL password verifiers can now use supported `SCRAM-SHA-256` verifiers or PostgreSQL `md5` secrets in addition to cleartext credentials. This lets credential-management workflows retain the server's stored representation where the authentication path supports it. (#5865.)

The configured authentication policy still applies. The default `pgsql-authentication_method=3` requires SCRAM and rejects MD5 credentials. Using an MD5 secret requires policy level `1` or `2` and an MD5 challenge from the backend. SCRAM pass-through requires successful SCRAM authentication from the application and a byte-identical verifier, including its salt, on each backend that user reaches.

### Query-rule selection of permanent forwarding

A MySQL query rule can now request a transition to permanent fast-forward mode with the Boolean attribute `{"switch_to_fast_forward":true}`. This lets routing policy select connections that should subsequently use direct forwarding.

The transition applies to a normal text query using the final selected hostgroup. If the client's protocol state cannot safely be carried into forwarding, the transition is rejected and the client connection is closed. This includes compressed connections, requests that cannot be reconstructed, and connections with another command already queued. Mirror and prepared commands do not consume this action. (#6156, #6440.)

The following are some highlighted updates with the newest release for InfluxDB 3. Learn more via our full [Release Notes](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb3/core/release-notes/#v3122). 

## Updates

### Core

#### Features

- **`influxdb3 debug catalog repair`**: This offline command, added in v3.11.6, is now also available on 3.12.2. It repairs a catalog that fails to load because of a duplicate table name or a reused table or database ID. Stop every node before you run it with `--execute`.
- **Processing engine Python updated to 3.13.18**: Picks up the security fixes released since 3.13.15.

#### Bug fixes

- **Queries that exceed memory limits returned `500`**: The HTTP query endpoints now return `429 Too Many Requests` when a query exhausts the DataFusion memory pool. Previously, they returned `500`. For CSV, JSON, and JSON Lines output, this applies when the query fails before it returns any rows. An error after the first rows still ends the HTTP `200` response early. Some Core queries still return `500`, such as a query on a table that runs out of memory while deduplicating data. Enterprise already mapped resource-exhaustion errors to `429`.
- **Catalog deadlock when checking a deleted table**: Checking whether a table is deleted now takes the catalog lock once. Previously, a catalog change that arrived between its two reads could deadlock the catalog.
- **WAL plugins received values under the wrong column names**: Rows passed to a WAL trigger's plugin now use the column names of their own record batch. Previously, when a flush held batches with the same columns in a different order, later batches used the first batch's column names.
- Other bug fixes and performance improvements

### Enterprise

All Core updates are included in Enterprise.
Additional Enterprise-specific updates:

#### Features

- **Faster [file index](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb3/enterprise/admin/file-index/) loading (Parquet engine)**: Loading a table's file index, including during a storage engine upgrade, now sorts each posting list once. Previously, every generation re-sorted each list it touched, so a table with many generations loaded slowly and used more memory.
- **Faster reads of compaction metadata (Parquet engine)**: Compaction and snapshot metadata files are now parsed in one pass, including during a storage engine upgrade. Previously, each was parsed twice.
- **Table index cache starts once the server is ready (Parquet engine)**: On ingest nodes, the table index cache now starts its background work when the server reports ready, instead of at the beginning of startup.
- **Fewer file downloads per query (upgraded storage engine)**: A query now downloads only the run set files whose key range covers the queried field family. Previously, it also downloaded files that held only the table's other field families.
- **Faster merging of overlapping files (upgraded storage engine)**: When a query merges rows from several files, each output column is now built in one vectorized step instead of row by row.

#### Bug fixes

- **Storage engine upgrade completed with unconverted Parquet files**: If a Parquet file fails every conversion attempt, the ingest node now reports `failed` in `system.upgrade_parquet_node`. The `last_message` column identifies the file and its error. The cluster upgrade also fails. To resume the upgrade, follow the [retry procedure](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb3/enterprise/reference/cli/influxdb3/manage/retry-upgrade-to-pacha-tree/#retry-after-an-ingest-conversion-failure). Previously, the node dropped the file and reported its upgrade as complete.
- **Storage engine upgrade stalled after an ingest node was removed**: The upgrade now drops a removed ingest node from its roster once its Parquet files are converted or absorbed. Previously, a removed ingest node held the cluster at `upgrading` forever.
- **Overwrites lost after a query node restart (upgraded storage engine)**: After a restart, a query node now reads gen0 files in the order they were written, so the latest write to a series and timestamp wins. Previously, a query could return the value from before an overwrite until compaction.
- **Query node could miss writes from a stopping ingest node (upgraded storage engine)**: A query node now keeps following an ingest node that is [`stopping`](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb3/enterprise/admin/node-lifecycle/) and fetches its remaining WAL files after it acknowledges the stop. Previously, the query node could stop fetching before the node flushed its last writes.
- **Trailing WAL fetch could hang after an ingest node stopped (upgraded storage engine)**: A query node's fetch of a stopped ingest node's remaining WAL files now completes. Previously, it could wait forever on files its workers had already fetched.
- **Nodes stopped applying compaction updates after falling behind (Parquet engine)**: A node that refreshes its view of compacted data no longer reads the detail of each generation the compaction removed. Previously, a node more than [`--compaction-cleanup-wait`](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb3/enterprise/reference/config-options/#compaction-cleanup-wait) behind the compactor failed every refresh with `generation detail not found` until it restarted.

Previously, the missing snapshot failed the cache initialization, and retention didn't run until the next restart.
- **Restarted node listed as stopped by its previous process**: A process that is shutting down no longer marks its node stopped once another process has registered under the same `--node-id`. Previously, a slow shutdown could mark the running replacement as stopped, and on the upgraded storage engine query nodes stopped following its WAL.

   The `web` service kept the theme defaults in a package-level map and merged the
   base and branding themes into that shared map on every `GET /themes/*` request.
   Concurrent requests therefore read and wrote the same map at the same time,
   which is a data race: it could corrupt the rendered theme, leak values between
   themes, or crash the service with a concurrent map read and map write.

   The theme defaults are now built fresh for each request, so no state is shared
   between concurrent requests.

## What's Changed

> ℹ️ **Heads-up for users of Compose as a library:** `Up` now runs its Create and Start phases as **a single plan over a single daemon snapshot**, for `up -d` ([#14290](https://github.com/docker/compose/pull/14290)) and interactive `up` ([#14305](https://github.com/docker/compose/pull/14305)), as `scale`, watch rebuilds and `start` already do ([#14291](https://github.com/docker/compose/pull/14291), [#14296](https://github.com/docker/compose/pull/14296)). The CLI behaves as before. If you call `api.Compose.Up` from your own program:
>
> * `Up` now validates its options first, with the same rules as the CLI flags: `UpOptions.Validate()` returns an `*api.IncompatibleOptionsError` (`errors.Is(err, api.ErrIncompatibleOptions)`) for `Start.Wait` combined with `Start.Attach`, and for a detached `Up` (no `Start.Attach`) combined with `OnExit`, `ExitCodeFrom` or `Watch`. Those combinations used to be silently ignored ([#14306](https://github.com/docker/compose/pull/14306)).
> * `Up` works on the project it is given and ignores `StartOptions.Project`.
> * The daemon is not observed again between the two phases: a container that exits after the plan is built is not started again, and one removed in between makes its start fail instead of being skipped. A planning error of the Start phase now fails before any container is created.
> * A foreground `Up` now gives a `use_api_socket` service its `/run/secrets/docker/config.json`, as `up -d` does, and shows the output of `pre_start` hooks.
> * The keyboard menu of an interactive `up` is no longer built by the library: set `NavigationMenu: true` **and** pass an implementation with `compose.WithNavigationMenu(...)`, otherwise no menu is displayed and a warning says so ([#14324](https://github.com/docker/compose/pull/14324)).
>
> Other changes to the library surface in this release: `DownOptions.Images` is now an `api.ImagePruneMode` (untyped constants still compile, a `string` variable needs a conversion) and an invalid value is rejected before `Down` removes anything ([#14149](https://github.com/docker/compose/pull/14149)); `compose.ServiceHash`, `compose.NetworkHash` and `compose.VolumeHash` are no longer exported, the helpers having moved to an internal package ([#14405](https://github.com/docker/compose/pull/14405)); `api.Compose` is now assembled from six smaller interfaces, with the same method set ([#14322](https://github.com/docker/compose/pull/14322)); `PushOptions.IgnoreMissing` is added.

# Release notes

Netdata v2.12.3 is a patch release to address issues discovered since [v2.12.2](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/releases/tag/v2.12.2).

This release makes the Agent detect a dead Netdata Cloud connection even while traffic keeps flowing, fixes use-after-free crashes when a stale node is removed while a child or plugin is still using it, stops children configured with `parent using h2o` from crashing on every connection, makes a negated IP in an access list take precedence over hostname matching, rejects malformed percent escapes in URLs, bounds MCP batch requests, removes global SQLite stalls, fixes crashes when obsolete charts are cleaned up while they are still being read, keeps the Agent from hanging at startup when a `dbengine` tier cannot be created, keeps Parents using the `ram` or `alloc` storage modes from shifting their children's history after a gap and from crashing on multi-node metric correlations, lets SNMP and other virtual nodes go offline again when their collector stops reporting them, makes PowerStore charts show the values the array reports instead of zeros, makes the eBPF plugins ignore directory overrides from the environment when they run with elevated privileges, and reloads host labels from the configuration file the Agent actually loaded.

## Streaming and Netdata Cloud

- Fixed the MQTT keepalive of the Cloud connection. It was only checked when the connection was idle, so a link with steady inbound traffic never noticed an unanswered ping and could stay stalled indefinitely. The ping and acknowledgement deadlines also followed the wall clock, so a clock step caused a false ping timeout or delayed detection, and on boards without an RTC acknowledgements never timed out before the first NTP sync. Deadlines now use a monotonic clock, and a dead connection is detected 60 seconds after an unanswered ping ([#24427](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24427), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag))
- The Agent's HTTPS client for Netdata Cloud now checks the chunk sizes of chunked responses strictly and caps such responses at 1 MiB. A malformed or very large chunk size could make the Agent exit while allocating memory for it ([#24483](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24483), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag))
- Fixed use-after-free crashes when `netdatacli remove-stale-node` or the orphan and ephemeral host cleanup removed a host that was still in use, either by a child reconnecting to it or by a plugin that had it selected as a virtual node. A child that reconnects during a removal is now asked to retry, and a virtual node selected by a plugin is reported as online and left alone ([#24353](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24353), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag))
- Removed the `[stream] parent using h2o` option. The h2o web server was removed in v2.7.0, and since v2.8.0 a child with this option enabled crashed on every connection attempt to its Parent. A `stream.conf` that still sets it is accepted and the option is ignored ([#24426](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24426), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag))

## Web server and APIs

- Access lists: a client whose IP matches a negated entry, such as `!203.0.113.7` in `allow connections from = !203.0.113.7 *`, is now denied without its hostname being checked against the list. This applies to every access list in `netdata.conf` when DNS checks are enabled, including the default `heuristic` mode for lists with a wildcard ([#24404](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24404), [@ArjunD3456](https://github.com/ArjunD3456))
- URLs with malformed percent escapes are now rejected with HTTP 400. A `%` had to be followed by two hex digits but was not checked, and a URL that failed to decode was served using the part decoded so far, so `/api/v1/info%zz` was answered as `/api/v1/info`. A request containing a literal `%` that is not followed by two hex digits, such as `?x=100%`, now gets 400 ([#24248](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24248), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag))
- The MCP API key and the management API key are now compared in constant time, so response timing no longer reveals how close a guessed key is ([#24418](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24418), [@ArjunD3456](https://github.com/ArjunD3456))
- MCP: JSON-RPC batches are limited to 64 requests and 16 MiB of responses, and WebSocket messages to 1 MiB, the same as HTTP requests. Requests whose id is not a string, number or null are rejected ([#24425](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24425), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag))
- `X-Forwarded-For`: the Agent now keeps only the first address of the header, and only when it is a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address. This is the forwarded client address shown in the access log and in the audit entries of dynamic configuration changes. Other values, such as `unknown`, are dropped ([#24452](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24452), [@ArjunD3456](https://github.com/ArjunD3456))
- Registry: the `netdata_registry_id` identity is now read only from the `Cookie` header, not from anywhere else in the request, such as the query string. This affects only Agents with the registry enabled, which is off by default ([#24494](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24494), [@ArjunD3456](https://github.com/ArjunD3456))
- Claiming: a request to `/api/v2/claim` or `/api/v3/claim` with a wrong key no longer regenerates the claim challenge, so it cannot interrupt a claim an administrator is making. The challenge is still regenerated at startup and after a claim with a valid key ([#24531](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/24531), [@stelfrag](https://github.com/stelfrag))
